A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Multipole Attention work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices B–C to v2 Appendices E–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBenchV2 and GSM-Infinite evaluations, GPU attention benchmarks and clustering-runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds LongBenchV1 evaluations, hyperparameter ablations and comparative runtime measurements in Appendices B–D.

M1.justification: The clustering, centroid-based retrieval and approximation, windowed RoPE, online updates and hierarchical algorithm remain unchanged. Testing another model and varying existing hyperparameters do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds LongBenchV1's 14 non-synthetic tasks spanning single-document and multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning and code. This substantially extends the retained LongBenchV2 and GSM-Infinite coverage to non-reasoning long-context evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds evaluated comparators DuoAttention and TOVA alongside Squeezed Attention. Table 6 also adds Squeezed Attention to the runtime comparison, where v1 benchmarked Multipole Attention against FlashDecoding. The original accuracy comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: The added LongBenchV1 evaluation introduces Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, simulated decoding of the last 50 prompt tokens, temperature 0, and 95% Multipole Attention sparsity with metadata-adjusted comparator budgets. Appendix C adds centroid-ratio and block-size sweeps. Existing reasoning-evaluation and kernel-benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C directly tests sensitivity to two central clustering choices: five centroid-to-token ratios and four block sizes on LongBenchV2 Short with Qwen3-8B and token budget 128. These analyses were absent from v1; the existing hierarchical comparisons and clustering-overhead analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged across three trials and retain 500 warmup and 500 measurement runs for kernel benchmarking. v2 introduces no new seed-reporting, confidence-interval, error-bar or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports average scores of 42.5 for Multipole Attention, 39.6 for Squeezed Attention, 33.1 for TOVA and 27.2 for DuoAttention, versus 47.0 for full attention. Tables 4–6 add sensitivity results and Squeezed Attention speedups. Original benchmark and runtime results remain unchanged; Table 6 redisplays Multipole Attention's existing 90% sparsity results.

T1.justification: The centroid definitions and attention expressions in Equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. Neither the revised main text nor the added appendices introduce new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about multipole approximation, fast online clustering, hierarchical lookup and up to 4.5x attention speedup. The additional evaluations support the work without redefining its central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning applicability beyond reasoning, hyperparameter tradeoffs and comparable latency to Squeezed Attention. Section 7 replaces the restricted-evaluation limitation with centroid-storage overhead. Table 3 also qualifies TOVA's GQA memory footprint. Appendix C's general trend explanation is stronger than its non-monotonic ablation results support.

D1.justification: Appendix B identifies the DuoAttention evaluation implementation and documents the decoding simulation, temperature, sparsity and centroid settings for the new experiment. The original implementation descriptions, clustering defaults and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LongBenchV1, TOVA's Transformers Are Multi-State RNNs paper and DuoAttention. These support the added evaluation and comparisons; the existing related-work discussion and positioning against clustering and retrieval methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include citation-format normalization, small grammatical edits, added results discussion and new Appendices B–D. The previous runtime appendices become E–F, while the main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn, and new Tables 3–6 display the additional evaluations. Figure 4 moves within the main text, while existing supplementary runtime material is redistributed and its tables renumbered 7–9. The overall visual format and existing result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The new evaluations improve assessment of applicability, parameter sensitivity and the accuracy–latency tradeoff, particularly through the direct Squeezed Attention runtime comparison. The original evidence is preserved. However, the ablation explanation overgeneralizes its trends: Table 4 reports 38.5 at ratio 1/32 versus 38.1 at the chosen 1/16. The additions provide a useful but limited overall quality gain.
